title: fix(workers): avoid provisioning during failed-dispatch cleanup

commit.messageHeadline: fix(workers): clean up allocations without replaying provisioning
fix(workers): fence local authority before resolving cleanup
fix(crabbox): retain cleanup responsibility through conflicts
fix(workers): retain cleanup authority across runtime failures
fix(testing): finalize worker profiles before teardown

No predecessor PR is attributed. ## Merge readiness ⚠️ **Ready for maintainer review - 4 items remain** Keep open. Current main still replays provisioning for null-lease cleanup, while this maintainer-owned PR replaces that path with allocation-only resolution and retains canonical teardown; no introduced correctness defect was established. **Priority:** P1 **Reviewed head:** `842f8783535927f891e30bf2249f5e2f98ffc834` **Owner decision:** Required. See [Decision needed](#decision-needed). ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | The patch has a coherent owner-boundary repair and focused coverage, with a remaining maintainer decision on the beta plugin contract. | | **Proof confidence** | 🌊 off-meta tidepool | Not applicable: Repository state identifies this as a MEMBER-authored PR, so the external-contributor proof gate does not apply; the supplied body excerpts nevertheless describe matching-package fault-injection and exact-head validation. | | **Patch quality** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Not applicable | Not applicable: Repository state identifies this as a MEMBER-authored PR, so the external-contributor proof gate does not apply; the supplied body excerpts nevertheless describe matching-package fault-injection and exact-head validation. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 6 items | Current-main bug remains: Current main has no allocation resolver in the WorkerProvider contract and both null-lease cleanup paths call resumeProvision, which can invoke provider provisioning before destroy.
Proposed lifecycle owner: The branch validates the allocation result, publishes only leaseId and sharedHost, and reuses the existing provider destroy path without manufacturing transport or enrollment state.
Provider contract and sibling adoption: The required resolver is documented in the public WorkerProvider type, validated at registry registration, and implemented by the Crabbox, paired-device, and static-SSH providers. | | **Findings** | None | None. | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together Cloud-worker dispatch persists an operation before a provider returns its lease; cancellation and restart cleanup consume that persisted state. The Gateway now asks the provider for a cleanup handle, then sends it through the existing stop and destroy lifecycle instead of restarting setup or enrollment. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Cloud dispatch] --> B[Durable operation record] B --> C[Failed or lost lease response] C --> D[Cleanup requested] D --> E[Provider resolves cleanup handle] E --> F[Gateway stop and teardown] F --> G[Destroyed or retryable record] ``` ## Decision needed | Question | Recommendation | |---|---| | Should OpenClaw accept resolveAllocation as a required beta WorkerProvider API, intentionally rejecting installed beta providers that have not migrated? | **Confirm the beta cutover:** Keep resolveAllocation required, preserve the no-provisioning teardown invariant, and communicate that beta worker providers must implement it. | Why: The repair needs a resolver to avoid unsafe provisioning fallback, but making a public beta plugin contract mandatory deliberately changes registration behavior for third-party beta providers. ## Before merge - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - The required public WorkerProvider resolver will reject external beta plugins that have not adopted it; maintainers should explicitly affirm the intended beta cutover and operator communication before merge. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - The profiler path relies on Vitest runner behavior; this read-only sparse checkout has no installed Vitest dependency source to independently inspect that contract, although the supplied exact-head CI and subprocess evidence claims cover it. - [ ] **Complete next step (P2)** - A maintainer must confirm the deliberate beta plugin-contract compatibility boundary; there is no narrow mechanical repair finding to dispatch.

The required-resolver decision was made before implementation and is recorded in the [maintainer-approved bounded design](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/132126). The approved scope includes a **required allocation-only resolver**, migration of Crabbox, paired-device and static-SSH producers together, and no teardown fallback into provisioning. This is the intended unshipped SDK cutover: prerelease providers missing the method must update before registration succeeds. Latest stable `v2026.7.1-2` predates this worker-provider API; no stable provider contract is being silently removed. No new transition/compatibility path is requested or added. This addresses the decision and Rank-up item in the latest review without reopening the already approved choice.

The storage change is the approved timing/ownership change within existing fields and the existing provisioning-to-draining representation, not a new schema/table/column/state/version. The linked issue records that material-persistence approval and the rollback caveat; schema compatibility alone is not a claim that the old provisioning-replay behavior is safe.

The latest review is now for `11c45558c457d1a8bc73a7daac65a6bdf667d1bd`; its required-contract/Rank-up decision remains covered by that prior explicit approval, not a new inferred approval. Latest stable was rechecked on August 29 UTC and is still `v2026.7.1-2`.

Production growth is **+96/-47, net +49**, with **+525/-94 tests/test support** and **+6/-4 docs**. This is the bounded new cleanup-identity capability and its ownership boundary: required public contract, three actual producer implementations, validation of untyped identity results, and current-owner checks around awaited publication/teardown. The implementation removes both calls from cleanup back into provisioning and the obsolete late-bootstrap skip. Reusing `provision` with a mode flag, an optional resolver/fallback, or fabricated transport fields would retain the ownership defect rather than absorb it. Existing stop/destroy and store transitions are reused; there is no parallel teardown owner. The CI fencing follow-through adds no net executable production statements—only two invariant-comment lines. The provider boundary is the concrete reason this coherent repair has positive production LOC.

CI did catch a real local-fencing order regression in the first candidate. The corrected owner fences cached authority before provider lookup/resolution; 404 distinct owner/producer/sibling tests passed, including shared/unknown-host ACK requirements and bound unreported nodes. The startup fixture now waits on allocation resolution rather than the intentionally removed provision replay. The correction is published, fresh restricted P0 autoreview is clean, full changed checks/build/package validation passed, and exact-head [CI run 33231203001](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33231203001) is green. The inherited checkout fixture fixes were taken from their canonical main repairs, without weakening assertions or deadlines.

This is **not yet a land-ready claim**: matching-package live acceptance and native review/prepare/merge remain in progress. The body distinguishes historical scoped no-create/repeat/restart proof from the later real allocated-VM failure/cleanup proof, and records the experimental-backend, key-mismatch and real-Chrome UI limitations. Contributor-gate labeling does not waive those limits.
